newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Treasury attacks parliament on budget vote.
newsitem.headline: Israel Treasury attacks parliament on budget vote.

text.p: Israel's Treasury on Sunday criticised the parliamentary finance committee for rejecting key components of the government's 1997 budget while claiming it supports spending reductions in principle.

"The question is what alternatives are members of parliament proposing in order to achieve the required cuts," the Treasury said in a statement. "Or is it enough for the MPs to simply reject existing proposals that were already approved by the government?"
The Treasury warned that if parliament did not approve all the cuts, "the economy will find itself in crisis".

The statement came after the finance committee rejected a proposed means test for determining child allowances. The test was intended to reduce child payments by 850 million shekels annually and constituted a major portion of the 4.9 billion shekels in overall spending cuts slated for next year.
The committee has yet to approve two other budget-cutting measures.
One to save 600 million shekels by raising charges for visits to the doctor is being revised in the face of parliamentary opposition.
The other, to reduce subsidies for new factories in development zones, has been debated in committee and has met heavy opposition.
Parliament has until December 31 to approve the 190.8 billion shekel budget package.
Opposition to the cuts has come from both the coalition and opposition parties on the grounds that they hit lower-income groups hardest.
